pressing.definition: The process of squeezing grapes to extract their juice.

fermentation.definition: A state of agitation or turbulent change or development.

maceration.definition: Softening due to soaking or steeping.

racking.definition: Causing great physical or mental suffering.

fining.definition: A production process in which selected substances are used to help remove suspended particles or unwanted components from wine.
fining.exampleUsage: The industry glossary describes fining as a clarification process.

filtering.definition: Using a filter to separate unwanted parts from physical material, transmitted information, or stored data.

aging.definition: Acquiring desirable qualities by being left undisturbed for some time.
aging.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Aging" in an educational description.

blending.definition: The act of blending components together thoroughly.

bottling.definition: The production stage in which finished liquid is placed into bottles and sealed.
bottling.exampleUsage: The factory diagram shows bottling as the final packaging stage.

wine-press.definition: A device presses grapes to separate their juice, which is then fermented into wine.
wine-press.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Wine Press" in an educational description.

fermentation-tank.definition: A vessel used to hold liquid while controlled fermentation takes place.
fermentation-tank.exampleUsage: The winery diagram labels the fermentation tank.

oak-barrel.definition: A wooden barrel made from oak and used for storage or aging in some food and beverage production.
oak-barrel.exampleUsage: The exhibit shows an oak barrel used in traditional storage.

stainless-steel-tank.definition: A large corrosion-resistant metal vessel used for storage or processing in food and beverage production.
stainless-steel-tank.exampleUsage: The production area contains several stainless-steel tanks.

crusher.exampleUsage: The crusher was used during the activity.

destemmer.definition: A machine used in grape processing to separate berries from stems.
destemmer.exampleUsage: The production diagram shows a destemmer before the crushing stage.

pump.definition: A machine used to move wine or juice between containers.

hydrometer.definition: A measuring instrument for determining the specific gravity of a liquid or solid.
hydrometer.exampleUsage: The hydrometer was used during the activity.

ph-meter.definition: An electronic device measures a solution’s acidity or alkalinity by sensing hydrogen-ion activity and reports the result on the pH scale, typically from zero to fourteen.
ph-meter.exampleUsage: The ph meter was used during the activity.

corking-machine.definition: A machine that inserts cork closures into bottles during packaging.
corking-machine.exampleUsage: The bottling line includes a corking machine.

french-oak.definition: Oak wood from France, commonly used to make barrels for aging certain foods and beverages.
french-oak.exampleUsage: The barrel display distinguishes French oak from other oak sources.

american-oak.definition: Oak wood from North America, commonly used to make barrels for aging certain foods and beverages.
american-oak.exampleUsage: The exhibit includes barrels made from American oak.

toasting.definition: Cooking to a brown crispiness over a fire or on a grill.

char.definition: A human female employed to do housework.

new-barrel.definition: A barrel that has not previously been used for aging or storing a product.
new-barrel.exampleUsage: The storage chart distinguishes a new barrel from a previously used one.

used-barrel.definition: A barrel that has already been used for aging or storing a product.
used-barrel.exampleUsage: The cellar inventory marks which barrels are used barrels.

micro-oxidation.definition: A controlled production technique in which very small amounts of oxygen are introduced over time.
micro-oxidation.exampleUsage: The textbook describes micro-oxidation as a controlled production technique.

lees.definition: The sediment from fermentation of an alcoholic beverage.

sur-lie.definition: A French term meaning that a wine is kept in contact with the sediment of yeast and other particles after fermentation.
sur-lie.exampleUsage: The glossary defines sur lie as aging in contact with fermentation sediment.

b-tonnage.definition: The total weight or mass of something, stated in tons.

red-wine.definition: An alcoholic drink made by fermenting dark grapes with their skins, which give it a red or purple color, tannins, and distinctive flavors.
red-wine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Red Wine" in an educational description.

white-wine.definition: A pale yellow to golden wine made by fermenting the clear pulp of grapes. It usually comes from green-skinned grapes, but red grapes can also be used when their skins have little contact with the juice.
white-wine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "White Wine" in an educational description.

ros-.definition: An artificial language for international use that rejects all existing words and is based instead on an abstract analysis of ideas.

sparkling.definition: Containing bubbles of carbon dioxide, especially in wine.

dessert-wine.definition: A sweet wine commonly served with dessert or at the end of a meal. It is often made from grapes harvested late, dried, affected by noble rot, or otherwise concentrated in sugar.
dessert-wine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Dessert Wine" in an educational description.

fortified-wine.definition: Wine strengthened by adding a distilled spirit, usually grape brandy, during or after fermentation; this raises its alcohol level and can alter its flavor and stability.
fortified-wine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Fortified Wine" in an educational description.

natural-wine.definition: An informal wine-industry term generally used for wine made with minimal intervention, although there is no single universal legal definition.
natural-wine.exampleUsage: The course notes explain that 'natural wine' has no single universal definition.

orange-wine.definition: A wine made from white grapes using extended contact with grape skins, giving an amber or orange color.
orange-wine.exampleUsage: The textbook defines orange wine by its skin-contact production style.

ice-wine.definition: A sweet wine traditionally made from grapes that freeze naturally on the vine before pressing.
ice-wine.exampleUsage: The geography lesson notes that ice wine is associated with cold-climate vineyards.

port.definition: Sweet dark-red dessert wine originally from Portugal.
